title: MovieChat: From Dense Token to Sparse Memory for Long Video Understanding
layout_note: Three columns: left, a film strip with a sliding window feeding a visual feature extractor, frame-level features and a short-term memory bar in a loop; centre, one large rounded panel 'Memory Consolidation' showing three steps; right, a long-term memory bar above Q-Former, projection layer and a wide LLM bar with Question and Answer boxes.
grouping: Memory buffers are purple-filled bars holding dash-dot token cells; the consolidation steps are grouped in one large beige rounded panel; a framed legend at the bottom keys the two line styles. The right column has no container.
shapes_depth: Flat shapes: purple rounded bars with dash-dot rounded token cells (x1…xK, B1…BG), beige trapezoids for the feature extractor V and projection layer P, a dark-teal diamond 'if full', teal rounded boxes for Question and Answer, a light-blue 'Extend Positional Encoding' bar, a wide light-grey LLM bar. Similarity scores are circles shaded from pale to dark orange with values under them; the merge is two pink cells joined to one taller mauve cell by lines of different thickness.
proposed_highlight: Memory Consolidation, the contribution, is the largest and only filled panel in the centre, with its three steps drawn on token cells; the two memories it moves between sit on either side as purple bars.
lesson: Put the operation that moves data between two stores in the centre as the largest panel, with the two stores as same-colour token bars on either side, and draw its steps on the tokens themselves (pairs, scored circles, a weighted merge).
notes: Venue written as arXiv: the arXiv PDF states no venue; remembered venue CVPR 2024 (unverified). year = arXiv preprint year. flow 'mixed': bottom to top from the film strip to short-term memory, left to right into consolidation and long-term memory, then top to bottom down the right column into the LLM. Symbol labels (x_t, B_n, calligraphic S, L, V, P) name the representations; there are no formulas. Film frames are embedded images (photo_share). Equation element = the symbol labels.

arrangement.units: one composition in three columns; only the centre consolidation panel is enclosed (beige rounded rectangle); a framed legend box sits bottom-centre
arrangement.inputs_as: a film strip of real movie frames at bottom-left with a grey rounded rectangle marking the non-overlap sliding window; a teal 'Question' box on the right
arrangement.shared: the Q-Former reads from both long-term memory and, in breakpoint mode, the current short-term memory and current frame via dashed lines

taxonomy.task: long-video question answering by a Q-Former-bridged LLM reading a short-term memory that is consolidated into a sparse long-term memory
taxonomy.note: training 'other': the figure draws no training; it shows the inference-time memory pipeline

insights.structure: Short-term memory (left) and long-term memory (right) are the same purple token bars on either side of a large central consolidation panel, and the model path (Q-Former, projection, LLM) runs down the right column.
insights.data: Frames are a real film strip, memories and the Q-Former input are rows of dash-dot token cells named x1…xK or B1…BG, and similarity scores are drawn as shaded circles with their values.
insights.emphasis: The consolidation panel is the largest element and the only filled container, holding three numbered steps drawn on tokens.
insights.flow: Numbered labels (1 apply consolidation, 2 clear S and initialization) mark the loop around short-term memory; solid lines are global mode and dashed blue lines breakpoint mode, keyed in a legend.
insights.avoid: A second purple bar above short-term memory (the cleared and re-initialised buffer) reads as a third memory, and the frame-level feature line bends round the left side up into short-term memory.

core.what: short-term and long-term memory drawn as matching purple token bars left and right of a large central consolidation panel that merges similar adjacent tokens

relations.form: two purple token-cell bars (Short-term Memory S at left, Long-term Memory L at top-right) with the consolidation panel between, arrows from short-term into the panel and from the panel to long-term
consolidation drawn on tokens: pairs of adjacent cells, a row of orange-shaded similarity circles with values, and the top pair merged into one cell by a weighted-sum glyph

short-term memory fills from frame-level features, an 'if full' diamond triggers consolidation, a return arrow clears and re-initialises the buffer; a circular 'repeat' glyph inside the panel for repeated merging
right column top to bottom: long-term memory, Extend Positional Encoding, Q-Former, projection P, LLM, Answer
in breakpoint mode, dashed blue lines bring the current short-term memory and current frame into the Q-Former beside the solid long-term memory line

channels.colour: purple = memory buffers (short-term, long-term, current S, current frame); beige = the consolidation panel and also the V and P trapezoids (two meanings); orange shade = similarity value; teal = question and answer; light blue = positional-encoding module; grey = LLM
channels.shape: purple bars of dash-dot cells = memories and token sets, trapezoids = feature extractor and projection, diamond = condition, circles = similarity scores, film strip = input video
channels.line: solid black = global mode, dashed blue = breakpoint mode (keyed); merge-line thickness = weight in the weighted sum
channels.frame: the beige rounded panel = the consolidation procedure; the Q-Former is a dash-dot frame around token cells, the same frame style as the memory cells

quality.strengths: The novel consolidation is the biggest element and its steps are drawn on the tokens (pairs, scored circles, weighted merge); both memories are drawn as token bars, not labelled boxes; the two inference modes are separated by line style and keyed; inputs are a real film strip with the sliding window drawn on it.
quality.weaknesses: The cleared/re-initialised buffer is drawn as an extra purple bar that reads as a third memory; the loop around short-term memory uses a line that bends round its left side; beige marks both the consolidation panel and the V/P trapezoids; the dashed breakpoint lines run long and cross the Extend Positional Encoding bar.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
